MITIGATED, NOT FIXED: both accounts now also exist content-addressed and immutable at prelude_6d9e1e0d.ndjson and prelude_2c87d457.ndjson, so neither set of bytes is lost and both remain hash-verifiable. I learned this by breaking it, and the repository's own guard caught me rather than me catching myself. THE OPERATOR'S CALL: accept a permanently-red entry with this record attached, or authorise a ledger rebuild (which is itself a violation of the append-only property this body exists to keep, and would be a far bigger decision than the defect it repairs). THREE OF THEM WERE INVISIBLE BECAUSE OF THIS GATE'S OWN CHECKS, and that is the lesson worth more than the build: (1) 'the lab's one non-GET route is carved out by name' counted ROUTES and never CALLERS -- true, and answering a different question than a reader takes from it; (2) 'NO VERDICT WITHOUT A RUN' proved only 'no verdict without a NUMBER NAMED exit_code' -- a hand-typed {exit_code: 0} produced a clean PASS row and the gate's very next check did exactly that; (3) 'THE GAP IS MEASURED' was `registered > 0 && typeof inLedger === 'number'`, a tautology, which is why it did not notice the headline count drifting in the same commit that wrote it. A SOURCE REGEX IS EVIDENCE ABOUT TEXT. Where the claim is about BEHAVIOUR, the rebuilt gate measures behaviour: it boots a server, issues a hostile cross-site request, runs processes, and hashes files and git state before and after. 20 checks, all green, and three of them fired on the first run.
builds.the_worst_one: POST /api/lab/run HAD NO CSRF FENCE. No Origin check, no Referer check, no token, and JSON.parse ignored content-type -- so the exact shape a browser sends with NO preflight (Content-Type: text/plain, or a JS-free auto-submitting form, which CORS does not govern at all) was accepted and acted on. Any page the operator had open could make his lab spawn gates and git worktrees in his own repository. AND THE FIX WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN HERE: viewer/command_center.cjs:1579 carries the same `x-uni-cc: 1` check, and ADR-PROD-015 specifies 'GET-only + ONE loopback-only POST ... requiring header x-uni-cc: 1' -- L5's architecture verbatim, with the fence made mandatory. L5 kept the body cap and the loopback bind and dropped the fence. Now enforced, plus a content-type check, plus one-run-at-a-time, plus a timeout on the child. PROVED BY ASKING A BOOTED SERVER: hostile cross-site POST -> 403.

builds.two_rows_never_one: BEFORE says verdict PENDING and evidence_class pending, which are the SCHEMA'S OWN WORDS for 'registered but not run'. AFTER requires a RUN TOKEN minted inside run() while a process was actually running, spent once, unreachable from a request. Refused with nothing, with an empty observation, with a verdict handed over directly, with a hand-typed exit code, and with a forged token. Two reasons and the second is the better one: it cannot touch the working tree (MEASURED -- git status --porcelain byte-identical before and after, and the worktree count unchanged), AND IT ANSWERS 'RUNNING, BUT NOT THE COMMITTED BYTES', which a run in your own tree cannot.
